newsitem.title: INDIA: Sterlite hopes for smelter decision soon.
newsitem.headline: Sterlite hopes for smelter decision soon.

text.p: Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd is awaiting a direction this week from the Tamil Nadu government on reopening its smelter, closed after suspected gas emissions, company officials said on Tuesday.
"We hope to get the direction (from the government) in a day or two," K. Ranganathan, general manager (commercial) of Sterlite Industries, told Reuters by telephone.

Earlier this month the firm was asked to shut its operations at the copper smelter at the southern port of Tuticorin for suspected gas emissions after more than 100 workers in a nearby factory were hospitalised.
The company strongly denies there was any gas leakage.
"There was no leakage of any kind from our plant," the company said in a statement.
Tarun Jain, a senior Sterlite official, told Reuters that an expert group set up by the state government to examine the suspected leak had submitted its report last week.
"We hope that the committee will take the same view as us," Jain said.
The smelter, with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes, began operations in December 1996.
Sterlite officials said that the closure was costing the company 25 million rupees ($700,280) daily.
